# DataCraft — Database Analyst

Studio: Analysis. Source: https://github.com/javy-fernandez/datacraft.

Use DataCraft for authorized database analysis. The browser edits the exact self-contained SQLite database opened from the private library and retains explicitly saved SQL companions. Other database providers and server/filesystem tools use the installed native application. Start with read-only queries; writes and schema changes must stay within the creator's authorized scope. Preserve SQL, source revisions, exact integers, blobs and NULL values. Keep connection credentials out of library packages. Work only in the assigned project and task working folder. Use studio-mcp for library access. Report a save only after the confirmed immutable revision; keep the exact pending snapshot through an interrupted acknowledgement without rerunning SQL, and preserve conflicts with native Save As.

Use `studio_run_native` with `appId: "datacraft"` and `args: ["--help"]` for the bounded command and input schema. `inspect INPUT.sqlite` opens the original installed DataCraft 0.11.0 GUI and returns its actual image. Inspect that image before choosing actions. `run INPUT.sqlite ACTIONS.json OUTPUT.sqlite` edits a separate local copy through original GUI controls. `new OUTPUT.sqlite [ACTIONS.json]` creates a genuine empty database through its SQL console. Outputs are exclusive. Commands have a private HOME and display; actions are limited to 100 inputs and 35 seconds, with printable ASCII typed text. The task-only native profile disables upstream autocomplete to avoid its cursor-bounds panic; the browser includes the bounds fix. The installed native binary remains unchanged.

Write actions and native files inside the assigned task folder. After an uncertain operation, inspect its preserved result before continuing; never repeat an edit over an existing output. Use `studio_save_native_project` for a new deliverable and `studio_save_input_revision` for the assigned exact input. A native local save or CSV download is not a library acknowledgement.

The browser retains the original Database Explorer, editable table grids, SQL consoles, script runner, CSV/TSV import, result exports and transaction semantics. Select Edit Data for an editable table; F2 edits a selected cell. Native grid Save/Ctrl+S and COMMIT save a consistent committed database; uncommitted transactions remain local until COMMIT and ROLLBACK creates no database revision. File/Save console as and Ctrl+S save SQL text alongside its database and reopen it on full reload. Original menus, status and modal dialogs carry save and conflict recovery. Never add duplicate save controls or wrapper banners.

Package one complete .sqlite, .sqlite3, .db or .db3 database (up to 256 MiB) and at most 100 selected UTF-8 .sql companions (16 MiB each). Checkpoint/close a hot native WAL before packaging; do not copy a live database without its journal. Browser SQLite sessions cannot attach arbitrary files, load extensions or publish uncommitted pages. Server connection management, provider-specific networking and filesystem backups stay in the native application. Browser acceptance covers SQLite, not browser access to all native database providers.

Integration status: verified for the native/browser/private-library/native loop in verification.json. Workstation image 0.2.1 is unchanged; immutable client 0.8.0 supplies native commands, packaging and previews.
